b: The Authority's protocol reference is available at berrienmca.org/protocols. The site carries the full Berrien County protocol set, searchable by title and full text, with patient report lines for receiving emergency departments. The set works offline once saved and reflects the current compilation at all times.

The Board has approved protocol modifications authorizing non-opioid analgesia and corticosteroid administration by the EMT Specialist under training prerequisites, affecting Sections 7-13 Pain Management, 3-3 Respiratory Distress, 4-5 Pediatric Respiratory Distress, and 1-6 Anaphylaxis. The package is pending Quality Assurance Task Force review in September 2026. Clean drafts are posted under Protocols Under Review.

t: Blood administration protocol approved and posted for comment
b: Berrien County protocol 7-31 Blood Administration received state approval on July 24, 2026 and is posted for review and comment under Protocols Under Review. Implementation follows the comment period and completion of agency accreditation under the protocol; the blood distribution framework remains in development. All EMS providers should know the indications for requesting blood response.

Eleven revised state protocols adopted by the Board on August 14 are in effect as of August 15, 2026: 1-3 Nausea and Vomiting, 6-3 Pediatric Tachycardia, 7-7 Do Not Resuscitate, 7-12 Oxygen Administration, 7-17 Patient Procedural Sedation, 7-25 MI POST, 8-24 Complaint Investigation and Resolution, 8-25 Disciplinary Action Appeal, and medication protocols 9-24R Fentanyl, 9-29R Ketamine, and 9-35R Morphine. The compiled protocol set and the protocol reference reflect the revisions.

The Board has adopted state protocol 7-29 Mechanical Chest Compression Device, effective August 15, 2026. Authorized devices are the Stryker LUCAS, Zoll AutoPulse, and Defibtech Lifeline ARM XR. Manual compressions remain the standard of care; device use is governed by the protocol.

t: Critical care epinephrine infusion package approved by the Board
b: The Board has approved a Berrien County protocol package establishing epinephrine infusion by credentialed critical care paramedics: a new infusion procedure at Section 7-32, a corresponding modification to 9-23R Epinephrine, and a modification to 8-17 Medical Control Privileges. The package has been submitted to MDHHS and takes effect upon state approval. The clean documents are posted under Protocols Under Review.
